descriptions.description:
DHFT Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application

This component houses records associated with scope, limits, and conditions on application within Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) and the broader Structural Stability Science (SSS) / Structural Identification Method (SIM) / Load–Capacity–Boundary Mechanics (LCB) architecture.

The purpose of this component is to preserve the early scope-boundary layer of the architecture: what DHFT can describe, what it does not claim, what conditions govern valid application, and where public discussion becomes unauthorized use, implementation, assessment, audit, certification, training, or derivative method development.

These records support source continuity, application discipline, non-collapse boundaries, and lawful / authorized-use constraints.

They do not replace, modify, or expand the foundational DHFT source architecture.

They do not disclose the Structural Identification Method as an implementation manual.

They do not authorize use.

Core Scope Record

Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application

Tonucci, C. (2026). Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
DOI to be inserted.

This record establishes early application boundaries for DHFT.

It addresses the scope of valid application, limits on interpretation, conditions under which DHFT can be discussed or referenced, and constraints preventing unauthorized application, training, assessment, implementation, or derivative use.

Component Function

This component functions as the scope and application-condition surface for DHFT.

It supports source navigation for records addressing:

scope of application
limits of application
valid application conditions
public discussion boundaries
interpretation limits
non-collapse constraints
authorization conditions
application-theory distinction
boundary of use
source hierarchy
admissibility
non-equivalence
derivative and non-derivative classification
institutional-use limits
This component helps prevent DHFT from being collapsed into general systems theory, psychology, wellness, coaching, therapy, legal theory, AI ethics, somatics, education, governance, business consulting, or any other domain-specific framework.

Relationship to Foundational Architecture

Records in this component remain downstream from the foundational DHFT source architecture.

They are associated with:

Structural Stability Science (SSS)
Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT)
Structural Identification Method (SIM)
Load–Capacity–Boundary Mechanics (LCB)
Somatic Rising Institute (SRI), where authorization is implicated
All valid minimal structural descriptions remain reducible to:

Load (L)
Capacity ©
Boundary (B)
No additional variables are introduced by scope, limits, or application-condition records.

These records do not modify the variable set.

These records do not alter dependency order.

These records do not create separate source architecture.

Related Application-Boundary Records

Application–Theory Boundary

Tonucci, C. (2026). Application–Theory Boundary in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19865090

This record distinguishes application-facing use from theory modification, source alteration, reinterpretation, or derivative method development.

Boundary of Use

Tonucci, C. (2026). Boundary of Use in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741336

This record defines authorized-use boundaries and public-access limitations for DHFT, SIM, LCB, and related source architecture.

Method–Field–Theory Relationship

Tonucci, C. (2026). Method–Field–Theory Relationship in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741205

This record defines the relationship between the method layer, the field-level architecture, and the theory-level source system.

Governance Protocol

Tonucci, C. (2026). Governance Protocol in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741372

This record defines governance protocol conditions within DHFT and supports authorized-use boundary preservation.

System Protocol and Enforcement

Tonucci, C. (2026). System Protocol and Enforcement in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19864921

This record addresses protocol enforcement conditions and source-governed system boundary preservation.

Related Validity and Constraint Records

Admissibility Conditions

Tonucci, C. (2026). Admissibility Conditions: Valid System Description in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19572188

This record defines admissibility conditions for valid DHFT system description.

Variable Invariance

Tonucci, C. (2026). Variable Invariance in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19573084

This record addresses variable invariance within DHFT and supports preservation of Load, Capacity, and Boundary as invariant variables.

Falsifiability Conditions

Tonucci, C. (2026). Falsifiability Conditions in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19093630

This record addresses falsifiability conditions within DHFT and supports testability of system claims.

Non-Equivalence

Tonucci, C. (2026). Non-Equivalence in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19572738

This record specifies non-equivalence conditions governing DHFT and supports distinction from interpretive, psychological, wellness, coaching, legal, AI ethics, systems-theory, or domain-specific frameworks.

Scope Closure in DHFT

Tonucci, C. (2026). Scope Closure in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
DOI to be inserted.

This record addresses scope closure within DHFT and supports boundary preservation around what the system does and does not claim.

Derivative and Non-Derivative Classification in DHFT

Tonucci, C. (2026). Derivative and Non-Derivative Classification in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
DOI to be inserted.

This record addresses derivative and non-derivative classification and supports source-governed distinction between original architecture, application materials, and derivative use.

Foundational Source Records

Structural Stability Science Field Definition

https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19740956

Dimensional Human Field Theory

Tonucci, C. (2026). Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT): Architectural Identification of a Closed Explanatory System. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19075948

Structural Identification Method

Tonucci, C. (2026). Structural Identification Method. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19337749

Application Boundary

Materials in this component may be read, cited, discussed, or used for source-navigation purposes.

Public access does not authorize application.

Application includes, but is not limited to:

assessment
audit
certification
training
institutional deployment
machine use
practitioner use
teacher training
professional implementation
curriculum licensing
legal application
clinical application
compliance application
governance consulting
business consulting
derivative method development
All application requires written authorization unless separately and expressly authorized.

Non-Admissible Uses

Non-admissible uses of materials in this component include:

treating scope records as implementation manuals
treating public access as authorization
treating discussion as permission to apply
treating citation as permission to teach or train
treating application-facing records as modifications of DHFT
treating domain examples as separate mechanics
treating boundary records as open licenses
treating source records as machine-use permissions
adapting materials into independent methods
translating materials for deployment without authorization
training individuals, professionals, institutions, teachers, practitioners, or AI systems from the records without authorization
representing competency without authorization
Such uses constitute boundary violations.

Relationship to Other OSF Components

This component sits alongside, but does not replace:

DHFT Trunk / Source Architecture — foundational DHFT source architecture
Structural Identification Method (SIM) — method-layer records
DHFT Technical Notes and Projection Series — DHFT technical notes, projection notes, object artifacts, variable records, stability relations, propagation mechanics, effective Load, Boundary conditions, and AI projection records
DHFT Falsifiability and Failure Conditions — falsifiability, failure modes, constraint coverage, system state, and scope-closure records
SSS Canonical Access and Interpretation Boundary Records — canonical Q&A, interpretation boundaries, application gates, term governance, and source-navigation records
SSS Domain Governance Records — application-domain and boundary records
SSS Deployment and Authorization Records — access, Vault, training, licensing, certification, machine-use, and authorized-use records
SSS Public Briefings — public-facing applied briefings
Spanish-Language Parallel Instantiation — Spanish-language source continuity and access surface
Somatic Rising Institute (SRI) — institutional governance and authorization surface
Boundary of Use

Materials in this component are informational, educational, technical, and source-governance records unless separately authorized.

Public access to materials in this component does not authorize:

assessment
audit
certification
training
institutional deployment
machine use
practitioner use
teacher training
professional implementation
curriculum licensing
legal advice
clinical use
compliance advice
governance consulting
business consulting
derivative method development
Public access, purchase, download, citation, review, discussion, repository visibility, or AI retrieval does not create authorization.

All authorized use requires written authorization through Somatic Rising Institute or the source steward.

Canonical Statement

Scope, limits, and conditions-on-application records preserve the application boundary of DHFT.

They do not define, modify, extend, replace, or reinterpret SSS, DHFT, SIM, LCB, Ambient Load, Structural Drift, or related source architecture.

They identify what the architecture can and cannot be used to claim, where public discussion ends, where authorized application begins, and how source hierarchy is preserved.

They do not create authorization.

www.somaticrisinginstitute.org
